head: The Jets need a win
paras: The Jets are winless in seven (0-5-2), while Carolina has won three straight. The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Winnipeg on Oct 17. Going in, the Jets are seventh in the Central (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Canes are first in the NHL.

The Hurricanes (1st) and the Jets (2nd) both create chances on the penalty kill. The Jets rarely ice the puck (5th), but take a lot of low-quality shots (29th). On the other side, the Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league, and allowed 2.33, the third fewest. The Hurricanes’ power play (9th) could do real damage against the Jets’ penalty kill (24th). On top of that, the Hurricanes roll four lines, but the Jets lean on their top six.

Kyle Connor (10 G / 4 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the Jets in scoring, and Cole Perfetti (6 G / 5 A / 11 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind. Sebastian Aho (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 15 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, and Logan Stankoven (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL.

Stuart Skinner (3-3-3 / .899 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Winnipeg. Carolina has two options in net: Pyotr Kochetkov (9-0-0 / .918 SV% in 9 GS) and Brandon Bussi (2-2-2 / .865 SV% in 6 GS). Kochetkov has started seven of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday, so Carolina could turn to Bussi to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Ehlers, Stankoven and Blake out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Rosén, Lowry and Iafallo. One more thing: the Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.

items.text: The Jets have been without Josh Morrissey since Oct 7.
The Hurricanes have been without Taylor Hall, Jordan Staal and Alexander Nikishin for several games.
Jaccob Slavin is set to play his 800th NHL game.
Seth Jarvis has scored in three straight games against his hometown Jets.

CAR.head: A big edge for the Hurricanes
CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. It’s on the Jets to make it a game, and they can if they get good looks.

WPG.head: The Hurricanes should be favored
WPG.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. The Jets’ best hope is getting good looks, plus a big night from Stuart Skinner.

calls.head: Ehlers’s line gets the soft minutes
calls.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Ehlers’s line (Ehlers, Stankoven and Blake) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Jets’ third line is Rosén, Lowry and Iafallo.

calls.head: The Hurricanes should tilt the ice
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Hurricanes have been the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Jets near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Hurricanes’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

calls.head: Stay out of the box, Jets
calls.body: The Jets’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Hurricanes’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Jets tonight.

calls.head: The Hurricanes roll four lines, the Jets lean on their top six
calls.body: On depth, Carolina is one of the league’s best, but Winnipeg is near the bottom. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Hurricanes.
